title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — October 23, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: anomalyco/opencode is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: anomalyco/opencode leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: anomalyco/opencode — 44 commits today, 2.4 above its current daily pace, with 45 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 232 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
laude-institute/rev-engine — No same-day commit after 49 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: OpenCode can prepare a summary before context fills
dailyInsight.insight: OpenCode has merged experimental background compaction: it can prepare a conversation summary while the current conversation continues, then use it when compaction becomes due. The option remains off by default.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The implementation keeps the summary aside until needed, preserving the current conversation prefix. It checks that the summary still fits the conversation and can fall back to ordinary compaction. If the summary is unfinished, compaction waits for it; unused background work still consumes tokens.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: For long coding sessions, preparing work early offers a different way to manage the compaction pause. Its value depends on whether the prepared summary is used and preserves the information needed to finish the task.

actions.label: Watch for a pinned workload comparison
actions.instruction: Before changing a production configuration, confirm a containing release and compare one disposable long task with background_compaction off and on. Record completion, summary fidelity, waiting time and all token usage. Keep the original configuration for rollback.
actions.effort: One bounded comparison after release containment is checked

receipts.title: Experimental background compaction implementation
receipts.supports: Merged implementation prepares, holds, validates and adopts a summary; unfinished work can still cause waiting.

receipts.title: V2 compaction configuration and limits
receipts.supports: Documentation names background_compaction, its opt-in status and the cost of unused summaries.

receipts.title: Scripted compaction test definitions
receipts.supports: Inspected test definitions cover default-off behavior, adopting a prepared summary and waiting for an unfinished one; not executed here.

confidence.basis: Merged code, subsequent configuration documentation and scripted test definitions inspected. No live task, suite execution or containing release verification was performed for this brief.

dailyInsight.limitation: This is an experimental source capability, not a measured reduction in pause time or total cost. A summary can be unused, invalidated or unfinished. No model-quality or workflow result was measured.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A pinned containing implementation cannot retain and adopt a compatible prepared summary as described, or matched tasks show the extra work does not improve the intended waiting-time tradeoff.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A containing release and matched long-task outcomes with complete token accounting, including discarded summaries.
